row: | DOC-A.1-170 | **SEARCH ALL statement — varying of the search index during the search operation**, §14.9.37 GR9 (§14.9.37.4), required + need not be documented (VOLUNTARY) | **A forward scan in occurrence order.** The initial setting of the search index is ignored: SEARCH ALL sets it to occurrence **1**, evaluates the WHEN condition, and on a false result advances it by one, until a WHEN is satisfied or the last element has been tested (`ControlFlowEmitter.EmitAllScan`). The bound is the table's maximum occurrence count, the CURRENT count of an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table, or the current capacity of an OCCURS DYNAMIC table. The last-element test happens BEFORE the advance, so the index never holds a value outside 1 through the last element — also on an unsuccessful search, where the AT END phrase sees it at the last element tested; an empty table (current count 0) is unsuccessful with no element tested and the index at 1. On success the index holds the occurrence number of the element that satisfied the WHEN. No binary search is performed, so a table whose ASCENDING/DESCENDING KEY data is not actually in sequence still finds an element that satisfies the condition when one exists. GR9 makes the final setting after an unsuccessful search undefined, so a program shall not rely on which in-range value is left. | `conformance:85/pb447_search_all_index_stays_in_table` |

row: | DOC-A.1-181 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph — allowable locale-names and literal values of the LOCALE clause**, §12.3.7 GR5 (§12.3.7.4), optional (documented if provided) | **Provided (2002 and later).** `LOCALE locale-name-1 IS {external-locale-name-1 or literal-4}` accepts the SAME set of identifications in both forms: a **locale tag** — any BCP-47 tag of a CLDR locale or of a culture .NET recognizes (`fr-FR`, `de-CH`, `sr-Latn-RS`, `zh-Hant`), a `-u-` extension allowed — or the root locale spelled `INVARIANT`, `ROOT`, `C`, `POSIX` or `und`. A **POSIX spelling** `ll_CC[.codeset][@modifier]` is normalized before use (`LocaleIdentification.Normalize`): underscores become hyphens, a `.codeset` suffix is ignored (the repertoire is always UTF-16), an `@modifier` that names a CLDR collation type becomes the `-u-co-<type>` extension (`de_DE@phonebook` is `de-DE-u-co-phonebook`), and any other modifier leaves a tag that names no locale. So `fr_FR`, `fr-FR`, `"fr_FR.UTF-8"` and `"fr-FR"` identify the same locale; the comparison is case-insensitive. The word form is limited to what a COBOL word can spell (no `.` or `@`), so `.codeset` and `@modifier` spellings need the literal form. literal-4 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal, not a figurative constant and not zero-length (`COBOLNET0898`); a locale-name declared twice is `COBOLNET1665`. **Availability is decided at RUN time, never at compile time**: any spelling compiles, and a locale that is not available (`LocaleIdentification.IsAvailable` — the root, a locale with CLDR collation data, a site `.tailor` file, or a culture .NET recognizes) raises `EC-LOCALE-MISSING` at the statement that uses it when that check is enabled. Before 2002 the clause is not recognized. | `unit:LocaleStateTests.ExternalIdentification_IsNormalized_PerDeterminationL1`; `unit:LocaleStateTests.Availability_IsTheOneKnownLocaleRule`; `conformance:2002/pb64t1_locale_declare` |

row: | DOC-A.1-187 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause — correspondence of the STANDARD-1 and STANDARD-2 phrases with the native character set**, §12.3.7 GR7 c) (§12.3.7.4), required + documented | **The identity on U+0000–U+007F.** Both phrases reference ISO/IEC 646 IRV (item 182), and each of its 128 characters corresponds to the native alphanumeric character with the same code: ordinal *n* of the standard set is native character U+(*n*−1), so `SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS ... row: | DOC-A.1-186 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, literal phrase — ordinal number of the characters not specified**, §12.3.7 GR7 k) 4. (§12.3.7.4), required + documented (the scheme, not each character) | **The ordinal number of every character is its collating position plus one, and the unspecified characters are numbered in the order GR7 k) 3. collates them.** A literal-phrase alphabet's coded character set contains every native character — 65,536 UTF-16 code units, for an alphanumeric and a national alphabet alike (`CodedCharacterSet.OrdinalCount`). The characters the literal phrase specifies take ordinals 1 through *n*, one per collating position in the order written (a THROUGH range fills successive positions; an ALSO group shares one position, and that ordinal names its first character, per GR7 k) 6.). The characters NOT specified then take ordinals *n*+1, *n*+2, … in ascending native code order, skipping the specified ones (`CodedCharacterSet.CharAt`). Worked example: `ALPHABET AL IS "Z" "Y" ALSO "W" "X"` has *n* = 3, so ordinal 1 is `Z`, 2 is `Y`, 3 is `X`, 4 is U+0000, 5 is U+0001, and ordinal 70 is `B` (U+0042, the 67th unspecified character). These are the ordinals `SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS … IN alphabet-name` and a numeric `CLASS … IN alphabet-name` literal use. The same in every edition. | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-194 | **Subscripts — mapping of an index value to an occurrence number**, §8.4.2.3 GR1 c) (§8.4.2.3.4), required + need not be documented (VOLUNTARY) | **The identity.** An index holds its 1-based occurrence number directly — a 64-bit integer, never a byte offset or displacement (the storage of an index is item 211) — so subscripting by `index-name-1` selects the occurrence equal to the index value (`BoundIndexRef`; `NumericRenderer.Visit`). `index-name-1 + integer-1` and `index-name-1 − integer-1` select the occurrence the index value plus or minus the integer names, computed without changing the index. row: | DOC-A.1-197 | **SYNCHRONIZED clause — positioning when neither RIGHT nor LEFT is specified**, §13.18.55 GR3 (§13.18.55.4), required + documented | **The item is positioned exactly where it would be without the clause: it begins at the byte immediately after the preceding item.** COBOL.NET treats every byte position as a natural boundary — a record is a typed .NET structure, not an addressable byte buffer, so an unaligned binary item costs no extra machine operations — and therefore performs no positioning, adds no slack bytes, and does not change the size of the item or of any containing group or REDEFINES (item 195). The same is true of `SYNCHRONIZED LEFT` and `SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT`: with a one-byte natural boundary an item both begins at the left byte and ends on the right byte of the boundaries that delimit it, so GR4 and GR5 are met with no adjustment, and the three forms lay out identically. Example: `01 G. 05 A PIC X. 05 B PIC S9(4) COMP SYNCHRONIZED. 05 C PIC X.` is 4 bytes, and `B` occupies bytes 2–3, with or without LEFT/RIGHT and with no clause at all. The same in every edition. | `conformance:2002/l1_byte_length_implicit_filler` |

row: | DOC-A.1-198 | **System-names — rules for the formation of a system-name**, §8.3.2.3 (§8.3.2.3.1), optional (documented if provided) | **Not provided.** COBOL.NET adds no restriction to the rules for forming a COBOL word: a system-name is formed exactly as any COBOL word of the target edition — letters, digits, hyphen, and (2002 and later) underscore, not beginning or ending with a hyphen or underscore, at least one letter, and at most 30 characters (COBOL-85), 31 (2002 and 2014) or 63 (2023), the length limit being `COBOLNET1567`. So a computer-name such as `123ABC` or `MY_BOX-9` is accepted. Which system-names are RECOGNIZED is a separate matter: device-names, switch-names and feature-names are a fixed list (item 189 and its neighbours; an unknown one is `COBOLNET2241`), code-names are items 183–184, and external-locale-names are item 181. | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-201 | **Text manipulation — stage of processing at which parameterized classes and interfaces are expanded**, §7.2 (the sentence is in §7.1), required + need not be documented (VOLUNTARY) | **At compile time, after all text manipulation.** COBOL.NET expands a parameterized class or interface when it BINDS the compilation group (`BinderDriver` → `OoExpansion`): for each `EXPANDS` specifier in a REPOSITORY paragraph it takes the parameterized definition's source text AS IT STANDS AFTER COPY, REPLACE and conditional compilation have been applied, substitutes each actual parameter for the corresponding formal parameter, and compiles the result as an ordinary, non-parameterized class or interface. So text manipulation can build or rename a formal parameter (a `REPLACE` that turns `ZZELEM` into `ELEM` before `CLASS-ID. ... USING ZZELEM` is seen gives the same class as writing `USING ELEM`), but a REPLACE never sees, and cannot alter, the text an expansion produces. Nothing is expanded at run time and no .NET generic type is used. Parameterized classes and interfaces exist from 2002 on; a class definition is rejected below 2002 (`COBOLNET0900`). | `conformance:2002/pb759_parameterized_class` |

record.notes: Voluntary row (A.1 201 need not be documented; A.1 cites 7.2 but cite.py --check 7.1 'The manner and time of expansion of parameterized classes and parameterized interfaces is defined by the implementor' -> OK §7.1 General). Probes probe/p201: pb759_parameterized_class.cob --std 2002 output identical to golden; pc2.cob (REPLACE ==ZZELEM== BY ==ELEM== + USING ZZELEM) output identical, i.e. REPLACE applied before expansion; --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900. PARTIAL: the golden pins expansion itself; the before/after ordering edge is witnessed only by probes, not by a committed test. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535.

row: | DOC-A.1-203 | **THROUGH phrase in the VALUE clause and the EVALUATE statement — collating sequence for a range when no alphabet-name is specified**, §14.7.8 rule 2, required + documented | **The PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE of the range's class — the same sequence a relation condition between the same operands uses.** A range of alphanumeric (or alphabetic) values, in a level-88 `VALUE … THROUGH …` or an `EVALUATE … WHEN … THROUGH …`, written without `IN alphabet-name`, is evaluated in the alphanumeric program collating sequence declared by `OBJECT-COMPUTER. … PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE` (§12.3.6), or in the native order (UTF-16 code-unit order) when none is declared; a range of national values uses the national program collating sequence (`… FOR NATIONAL`, 2002 and later), else the native national order (`CollatingSelection.ThroughRangeClass` → `CollatingSelection.ForComparison`). A national or alphanumeric GROUP conditional variable takes the sequence of its own class. A range whose first value collates after its second in that sequence is empty (with EC-RANGE-INVALID when that check is enabled). Example: with `PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS EB` where `ALPHABET EB IS EBCDIC`, the value `"_"` is NOT in `"Z" THRU "a"` (in EBCDIC `a` collates before `Z`), while with no PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE it is. Numeric ranges are algebraic (rule 1) and use no sequence. | `conformance:2002/pb398_range_in_alphabet`; `conformance:2002/pb728_level88_group_usage_collating` |

record.notes: cite.py --check 14.7.8 'When there is no IN alphabet-name phrase specified for the range, the collating sequence is defined by the implementor' -> OK §14.7.8 2). CollatingSelection.ThroughRangeClass = ForComparison over both ends (the relation-condition class rule). Probes probe/p203: th.cob --std 2023 (PCS EBCDIC, C='_'): 88 OUT, EV OUT, C<=Z, national no-PCS NEV IN; th85.cob/th85n.cob --std 85: with PCS 88 OUT/EV OUT, without PCS 88 IN/EV IN; thn.cob --std 2023 (PCS FOR NATIONAL IS NR = a _ Z): N88 IN, NEV IN, N>a. Goldens: pb398 legs C/E (no phrase -> PCS) and H (national no phrase -> native); pb728 V01 (national group under national PCS), V03/V04 (alphanumeric under alphanumeric PCS). Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB372.

row: | DOC-A.1-213 | **USAGE NATIONAL — size and representation of characters**, §13.18.60 GR8 (§13.18.60.4), required + documented | **Two bytes per national character position, uniform at every length: one UTF-16 code unit, stored MOST SIGNIFICANT BYTE FIRST (UTF-16BE).** `PIC N(2)` occupies 4 bytes (`FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH` 4, `FUNCTION LENGTH` 2), and a national-form numeric or numeric-edited item takes 2 bytes per symbol (`PIC 9(3) USAGE NATIONAL` is 6 bytes). The value of each position is the character's UTF-16 code unit — `A` is `00 41`, `é` is `00 E9`, `€` is `20 AC` — and this is the image seen through a REDEFINES, in an alphanumeric group that contains the item, and in a record written to a file. A character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is a surrogate pair and occupies TWO character positions, each half treated as a separate character exactly as §8.5.1.4 rule 2 requires, so a MOVE that truncates between the halves keeps only the first. There is no option to vary the size or representation per compilation unit. USAGE NATIONAL exists from 2002 on (`COBOLNET0900` below). | `conformance:2023/pb646_national_form_numeric_bytes`; `conformance:2023/l1_usage_display_character_size` |

record.notes: cite.py --check 13.18.60.4 'Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage NATIONAL' -> OK §13.18.60.4 8). Probes probe/p213 --std 2023: nt.cob BYTE-LENGTH(PIC N(2))=4, LENGTH=2; sequential record PIC N(3) 'Aé€' on medium = 00 41 00 e9 20 ac; MOVE N'A€😀' TO PIC N(3) keeps A, € and the high surrogate (LENGTH 3); ng.cob group N(2)'AB'+X'C' moved to X(5) -> bytes 00 41 00 42 43; REDEFINES of N'€' -> 20 AC; BYTE-LENGTH(PIC N)=2. Golden pb646_national_form_numeric_bytes pins 2 bytes/position UTF-16BE (BYTES=10, HIGHZEROS=5, EBYTES=12); l1_usage_display_character_size LEQN pins the national size. §8.5.1.4 rule 2 makes each surrogate half a character position. Consistent with DOC-A.1-188 / DOC-A.1-33 (UTF-16, one code unit per position). Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, A11.

row: | DOC-A.1-220 | **Variable-length data items — actual time when the resources used are freed**, §8.5.1.11.3, required + need not be documented (VOLUNTARY) | **Whenever the .NET garbage collector reclaims them — a time the program cannot observe and COBOL.NET does not fix.** No variable-length item has storage of its own to release: a DYNAMIC LENGTH elementary item is a managed .NET string, so the old value becomes unreachable when a new value is stored (a MOVE of "XY" over "ABCDEFGHIJ" leaves an item of length 2), and the collector reclaims it later. A dynamic-capacity table (`OCCURS DYNAMIC`, `CobolDynTable`) holds its occurrences in a managed array that grows by doubling and is NEVER shrunk: lowering the capacity (`SET … TO`, `DOWN BY`) only lowers the current count, keeping the removed occurrences' storage until the table is enlarged again — when each re-created occurrence is created afresh as a new occurrence, never with the value it held before — or until the table itself becomes unreachable. Freeing never affects a program's results. DYNAMIC LENGTH items and dynamic-capacity tables exist from 2014 on (`COBOLNET0900` below). | — |

record.notes: Voluntary row (A.1 220 need not be documented). cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' -> OK §8.5.1.11.3 7). Read CobolDynTable: GrowTo only Array.Resize upward (doubling, capped at MaxOccurrences), re-seeds occurrences _count..target with _seedAt; SetCapacity shrink sets _count only (no array shrink); ValueInitializer.cs:139 'the field is a native string' for DYNAMIC LENGTH. Probe probe/p220/vl.cob --std 2023: D=XY L=002; C(5)=7, SET CAP TO 2, SET CAP TO 5 -> C5=0 CAP=5; --std 2002 -> COBOLNET0900 for both. Collection timing is nondeterministic, so no test can pin it. Resource exhaustion is item 61 / kb/Work/PB1410, not this item. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535.
